newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Co-op sends warning to other predators.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Co-op sends warning to other predators.

text.p: Britain's mutually-owned Co-operative Wholesale Society on Friday sent out a warning to potential predators and pledged to continue to provide services to ordinary Britons.
"The CWS is not for sale to Mr Regan or to anyone else. The CWS has a strong future serving the everyday needs of ordinary people," said Graham Melmoth, chief executive of mutually-owned CWS.
A hostile 1.2 billion pound ($1.9 billion) takeover bid by 31-year-old entrepreneur Andrew Regan floundered on Thursday after legal action by the CWS and the withdrawal of key financial backing.
But the CWS was not in celebratory mood on Friday and said it would not be left out of pocket as a result of the recent events.

"We will not be out of pocket, other people will quite rightly pick up that tab," said Alan Prescott, the CWS executive leading an internal inquiry into how key papers ended up in the hands of a consortium mounting a bid for the Manchester-based supermarkets to funeral parlours group, founded in 1863.

For while the attempted bid has been canned, the CWS vowed to pursue legal moves against the predators after gaining a High Court extension of its earlier ban on the use of confidential CWS papers, leaked by suspended CWS manager Allan Green.

Mr. Justice Lightman said the case represented a "gross, wilful and disgraceful breach of confidence" and awarded punitive "indemnity" costs against Regan, his business associate David Lyons, Green and Regan's companies Lanica Trust and specially-formed bidding vehicle Galileo.

Christopher Clarke QC, the lawyer representing the CWS, had told the court how affidavits provided by Green, Regan and Lyons under the earlier order showed Green had passed on papers including CWS profit forecasts, the board budget and the board's defence plan to 1997 to Regan and Lyons.

Clarke said 32 documents had been handed over to the court, including the entire CWS membership list. He said Green's affidavit revealed he had met with Regan and Lyons on six or seven occasions and had handed over papers at most of these meetings.
The court was told Green had agreed he had exceeded his authority but believed at the time he was doing so in the best interest of CWS.

Clarke also said copies of some of the documents had been passed on to Galileo's City advisor British merchant bank Hambros and a long list of other organisations, including banks and financial institutions.

Retailer Sainsbury, Nomura, property consultant Healey and Baker, Leucadia National Corp., UBS, SocGen, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, HSBC Investment Bank, Lloyds Bank, Lloyds Bank Registrars, Bankers Trust, Avonwick Ltd, accountancy firm Price Waterhouse and Hillier Parker were all named.
Sainsbury had already said it was approached by Regan but returned any papers to Hambros. Goldman Sachs, Lloyds Bank and J.P. Morgan said they had also returned any documents they had been sent.
Hambros and City law firm Travers Smith Braithwaite have been added to the injunction. Hambros was not immediately available for comment.
Clarke also said that shareholders of Lanica had shown documents to British investment watchdog IMRO.

Earlier in the proceedings, when the lawyer representing Regan, Lyons, Galileo and Lanica said it was unfortunate the bid had never been presented to the CWS members, Lightman said "it was inevitable that it should be stopped due to the iniquitous manner in which it was done".
CWS has waged a high-profile defence, costing millions of pounds, with investment bank SBC Warburg since the bid attempt first surfaced in February.

This intensified last week when it suspended two senior managers, Green and David Chambers, for a serious breach of trust and later won a court order preventing the predators from using any of the information they had obtained through Green.

This effectively stopped the bid in its tracks, although it was not until Thursday that Regan and Galileo admitted defeat, blaming the fact that CWS chairman had not allowed them to put their proposals directly to CWS directors. These proposals were returned unopened and unread to Galileo.

CWS has also begun a private prosecution against Regan and Lyons as well as action accusing Green of theft. A preliminary hearing is due to take place in the City of London magistrates court on May 28. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
